title: Lattice sofa
words: Move a shape made of grid squares around a corner of a width-3 grid hallway using only grid moves and quarter turns. How many squares can it have?
math: Maximize $|P|$ over polyominoes movable by unit translations and $90^\circ$ rotations about lattice points around the corner of the width-3 lattice corridor.

title: Cross-polytopes in 4D
words: Every 4D convex body should have the corners of a regular cross-polytope on its boundary.
math: Prove every convex body in $\mathbb{R}^4$ has an inscribed regular cross-polytope.

title: Two-axis staircase sofa
words: A square pipe turns right and then up. Find the biggest solid that gets through.
math: Determine the optimal volume for the $1\times1$ corridor that turns about the $z$-axis and then about the $x$-axis.

title: Square-sum Ramsey numbers
words: Find the exact point at which every 2-coloring of 1 to N contains a same-colored square-sum clique of size 4.
math: Determine $\min\{N: \text{every 2-coloring of }[N]\text{ has a monochromatic }K_4\text{ in }S_N\}$, or prove none exists.

title: Prime Nim in polylog time
words: Decide whether a Prime Nim pile is losing in time polynomial in its number of digits.
math: Give an algorithm deciding $G(n)=0$ in time $(\log n)^{O(1)}$, or prove none exists under a standard assumption.

title: Seven-free three primes
words: Every large odd number should be a sum of three primes that never use the digit 7.
math: Prove every sufficiently large odd $N$ is $p_1+p_2+p_3$ with each $p_i$ prime and free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Lonely runners with prime gaps
words: Prove the lonely runner conjecture when all speed differences are primes.
math: Prove the lonely runner conjecture for speed sets $\{v_i\}$ with every $|v_i-v_j|$ prime.

title: Lonely runner, bounded speeds
words: Prove the lonely runner conjecture whenever all speeds are at most 10 times the number of runners.
math: Prove $\sup_t\min_i\|tv_i\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$ for all distinct $v_i\le10n$.

title: Emirp twins exist infinitely
words: Show infinitely many twin-prime pairs reverse to another twin-prime pair.
math: Prove infinitely many $p$ with $p,p+2$ prime and $\operatorname{rev}(p),\operatorname{rev}(p+2)$ prime with $|\operatorname{rev}(p)-\operatorname{rev}(p+2)|=2$.

title: Fire on the Sierpinski graph
words: With one firefighter per turn on the Sierpinski triangle graph, what fraction must burn as the graph gets bigger?
math: On the level-$n$ Sierpinski gasket graph with a fire at a corner and one protected vertex per turn, find $\lim_n \min |B|/|V|$.

title: Symmetric sofa
words: Find the best sofa that is symmetric under a half-turn.
math: Maximize area over centrally symmetric sets admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor.

title: Building a firebreak
words: Firefighters must build one connected wall, one cell per turn, each next to the last. Can they ever enclose the fire?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$, each turn add one protected cell 8-adjacent to the previous one. Decide whether a single fire can be enclosed, and for which build rates.

title: Parameterized Lean golf
words: Finding short proofs with basic tactics is hard in general, but maybe easy when the proof is short. Settle which.
math: Give an algorithm for intro/apply/exact/rfl proof search in time $f(k)\,n^{O(1)}$, or prove the problem W[1]-hard in $k$.

title: Many square-sum circles
words: Count the ways to arrange 1 to N in a circle with adjacent sums square. Show the count grows exponentially.
math: Prove $\log H(S_N)=\Theta(N)$, where $H$ counts Hamiltonian cycles.

title: Optimal origami base
words: Folders design animal shapes by packing circles on paper. Find the smallest paper needed for every stick figure with six legs or fewer.
math: For every weighted tree with $\le6$ leaves, determine the minimum square side admitting a uniaxial base (optimal circle–river packing), with certificates.

title: Sofa boundary is not holonomic
words: Show some piece of Gerver's sofa outline is not described by any linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients.
math: Prove some boundary arc of Gerver's sofa is not D-finite.

title: Sudoku needs guessing
words: Some minimal Sudoku puzzles cannot be solved by pure logical propagation. Show a positive share need trial and error.
math: Prove a positive fraction of minimal uniquely solvable $9\times9$ puzzles are not solved by singles, pairs and fish (a fixed propagation rule set).

title: Chiral 3D monotile
words: Find one 3D tile that fills space only non-periodically, using rotations only, never mirror images.
math: Find $T\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ that tiles by orientation-preserving isometries, admits no periodic tiling, and needs no reflections.

title: Stable blow-up
words: Show the 2026 Navier–Stokes blow-up still happens after any tiny change to the setup.
math: Prove the 2026 forced blow-up is stable under small smooth perturbations of $(u_0,f)$ in a suitable topology.

title: Spectre is a quasicrystal ground state
words: Find a finite-range pair potential whose only zero-temperature arrangement is the spectre tiling.
math: Construct a finite-range rotation-invariant pair potential for which every ground state is a spectre tiling, and prove it.

title: Cops on the hat tiling
words: Cops chase a robber across the tiles of a hat tiling. How many cops always catch the robber?
math: Determine the cop number of the adjacency graph of a hat tiling (it is at most 3 by planarity).

title: 5n+1 largest-factor convergence
words: Prove every orbit of the 5n+1 largest-factor map ends in a loop.
math: For $f_5(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(5n+1)$ (odd), prove every orbit is eventually periodic.

title: Caterpillar forests
words: Show that forests of caterpillar trees always have the distinct-edge-difference labeling.
math: For any forest of caterpillars with $m$ edges and $c$ components, find a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with distinct edge differences.

title: Keller monodromy
words: Describe how the preimages of a Jacobian counterexample swap around as you loop around bad points.
math: Compute the monodromy group of Alpöge's 3D Keller map as a branched cover over the complement of its discriminant.

title: Hat Ising free energy
words: Find the exact free energy of magnets on a hat tiling at the critical point.
math: Compute $f(\beta_c)$ for the Ising model on the hat graph in closed form.

title: Origami with no flat state
words: Characterize crease patterns where every crease must bend, yet nothing folds flat, using only angles at vertices.
math: Find a finite list of local vertex conditions that decides global flat-foldability for crease patterns with all vertices of degree 4.

title: Hat isoperimetry
words: Among groups of n hat tiles, how short can the boundary be? Find the exact constant.
math: For the hat adjacency graph, prove $\min_{|A|=n}|\partial A|\sim c\sqrt n$ and compute $c$.

title: Largest-factor Collatz, small cases
words: A Collatz-style map that halves even numbers but sends an odd number to the biggest prime dividing 3n + 1. Check that every start below a million falls to 1.
math: Let $f(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $f(n)=P(3n+1)$ for odd $n$, where $P$ is the largest prime factor. Show $f^{k}(n)=1$ for some $k$, for every $n<10^6$.

title: Doubled-twin constant
words: Assuming deep but standard conjectures, find the exact count of doubled twins up to x.
math: Assuming the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture, prove a lower bound $\gg x/(\log x)^4$ for doubled twins with $p$ and one other form prime.

title: Monster puzzle
words: Design a finite logic puzzle whose solutions have exactly the symmetries of the Monster group.
math: Find a constraint puzzle with $<10^6$ cells whose solution-preserving symmetry group is isomorphic to the Monster $\mathbb{M}$.

title: Wind-driven fire
words: On a grid, fire spreads each turn only east, north and south (the wind blocks westward spread). How few firefighters per turn can always trap a single burning cell?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$, burning cells ignite neighbours at offsets $(1,0),(0,\pm1)$ each turn; $k$ unburnt cells are protected per turn. Find the least $k$ that always yields a finite burned set.

title: Distant-force blow-up
words: The 2026 Navier–Stokes blow-up pushed fluid right where it broke. Make it break with a push kept far away.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ with $\operatorname{supp} f\cap B(x_*,1)=\emptyset$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes from rest blows up at $x_*$ in finite time.

title: Shuffle-sorting
words: Using any of the six 3-pile perfect shuffles each time, how many shuffles reach any reachable arrangement in the worst case?
math: Determine the diameter of the Cayley graph of the 3-pile shuffle group on $3n$ cards, asymptotically in $n$.

title: Square-sum spectra
words: Show the largest eigenvalue of the square-sum graph grows like a precise power of N.
math: Prove $\lambda_1(S_N)\sim cN^{1/4}$ and determine $c$.

title: T-junction sofa
words: A sofa comes up the stem of a T and must be able to leave by either arm. Find the biggest one.
math: Maximize area over sets admissible from the stem to each arm (separately) of a width-1 T-junction.

title: Benford orbits
words: The leading digits of largest-factor Collatz orbits should follow Benford's law.
math: Prove that for almost all $n$ the leading digits of $(f^k(n))_{k\le T(n)}$ satisfy Benford's law as $n\to\infty$.

title: Lean golf is hard to approximate
words: Not only is the shortest basic-tactic proof hard to find; even a roughly short one is.
math: Prove intro/apply/exact/rfl proof minimization admits no constant-factor approximation unless P = NP.

title: Spherical sofa
words: Find the biggest shape that turns a right-angled corner in a width-1 hallway drawn on a large sphere.
math: On the sphere of radius 10, determine the maximal area of a set admissible in the width-1 right-angled geodesic corridor.

title: Squares on a sphere
words: Every closed curve on a sphere should pass through the corners of a spherical square.
math: Prove every Jordan curve on $S^2$ inscribes a spherical quadrilateral with equal sides and equal angles.

title: Shuffle cycle census
words: For a k-pile perfect shuffle, how many cards come back home after exactly d shuffles?
math: For the $k$-pile out-shuffle on $kn$ cards ($i\mapsto ki \bmod (kn-1)$), count the points of exact period $d$ in terms of $kn-1$ and $d$.

title: Icosahedral monotile
words: Find a single 3D tile that fills space and forces five-fold, icosahedral symmetry in every tiling.
math: Find $T\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ tiling space such that every tiling by $T$ has icosahedral symmetry in its hull, or prove none exists.

title: Sudoku clue growth
words: Big Sudokus need more clues. Find how fast the minimum number of clues grows with the board size.
math: Let $c(n)$ be the least number of givens in a uniquely solvable $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku. Determine the growth order of $c(n)$.

title: Go on a torus
words: Go on a 7 × 7 board that wraps around. What komi makes the game fair?
math: Determine the perfect-play score of Go on $\mathbb{Z}_7^2$ (area scoring, positional superko).

title: Toroidal Go 9×9
words: Who wins Go on a 9×9 board that wraps around in both directions?
math: Weakly solve Go on $\mathbb{Z}_9^2$ with area scoring and komi $0$.

title: Prime Nim periodicity of differences
words: Show the gaps between consecutive Prime Nim losing positions are not eventually periodic.
math: Prove the difference sequence of $\{n:G(n)=0\}$ in Prime Nim is not eventually periodic.

title: Hat corona limit
words: Surround a hat by layers of hats again and again. The growing blob approaches a fixed shape. Find it.
math: Prove the scaled $k$-th coronas of a hat converge in Hausdorff distance and identify the limit shape.

title: Big factors of p² + p + 1
words: For primes p, show p² + p + 1 often has a very large prime factor.
math: Prove $P(p^2+p+1)>p^{1.5}$ for infinitely many primes $p$.

title: Two forbidden distances
words: Color the plane so no two points at distance 1 or √3 share a color. How many colors are needed?
math: Determine $\chi(\mathbb{R}^2;\{1,\sqrt3\})$.

title: Hat random walk diffusivity
words: A random walk across hat tiles should look like ordinary Brownian motion from far away. Find its exact spreading rate.
math: Prove the simple random walk on the hat adjacency graph satisfies an invariance principle with isotropic covariance $\sigma^2 I$, and compute $\sigma^2$.

title: Hat Ising universality
words: Magnets on a hat tiling should behave at their critical point exactly like magnets on a square grid.
math: Prove the hat-graph Ising model has critical exponents $\beta=1/8$, $\gamma=7/4$, $\nu=1$.

title: Square-sum paths from 1
words: Arrange 1 to N in a line starting with 1 so neighbours add to squares, for every large N.
math: Prove $S_N$ has a Hamiltonian path starting at vertex 1 for all $N\ge 25$.

title: 3D sofa ceiling
words: Put a finite, explicit cap on how much volume can turn the corner of a square pipe.
math: Prove an explicit $V_0<\infty$ such that every solid admissible in the $1\times1$ square corridor has volume $\le V_0$.

title: AP-free primes
words: Find the largest set of primes below x with no three in arithmetic progression.
math: Determine the growth of $\max\{|A|: A\subset\{p\le x\},\ A \text{ has no 3-term AP}\}$ up to $x^{o(1)}$ factors.

title: Analytic hyperoperations
words: Build one smooth family of operations from addition up through exponentiation that is analytic in all inputs.
math: Construct $a[s]b$, real-analytic in $(s,a,b)$ for $s\in[1,3]$, $a>1$, $b>0$, satisfying the recursion law and matching $+,\times,\uparrow$.

title: Doubled-twin sieve upper bound
words: Bound the number of doubled-twin quadruples up to x by the predicted count times at most 3.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: p,p+2,2p+1,2p+3\text{ prime}\}\le(3+o(1))\,\mathfrak{S}x/\log^4x$, with $\mathfrak S$ the singular series.

title: Largest-factor climbs
words: Show infinitely many starts climb above their own square before falling.
math: Prove $\max_k f^k(n)>n^2$ for infinitely many $n$.

title: Hyperoperation Goodstein
words: A Goodstein-style sequence using hyperoperations always ends, but ordinary arithmetic cannot prove it.
math: Define base-change on hereditary hyperoperation normal forms; prove the sequences terminate and termination is unprovable in PA.

title: Prime Nim table
words: Two players take turns removing a prime number of stones from a pile; whoever cannot move loses. List the losing pile sizes up to 120.
math: With moves $n\mapsto n-p$ ($p$ prime), show the zero Grundy values for $0\le n\le120$ are exactly $\{0,1,9,10,25,34,35,49,55,85,91,100,115\}$.

title: Beat the prism
words: Gerver's sofa, lifted to one unit tall, can turn a corner in a square pipe. Find a 3D shape with more volume that can still make the turn.
math: In the corridor $([0,1]\times\mathbb{R}\cup\mathbb{R}\times[0,1])\times[0,1]$ turning about the $z$-axis, find a rigid motion-admissible solid of volume $>2.2195\ldots$.

title: Prime-graceful forests
words: Label any forest so the edge differences are exactly the first m primes.
math: Prove every forest with $m$ edges has an injective $\ell:V\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ whose edge differences are $\{p_1,\dots,p_m\}$.

title: Prime Nim and Presburger
words: Show the losing positions of Prime Nim cannot be described by simple arithmetic with addition alone.
math: Prove the P-position set of the prime subtraction game is not definable in Presburger arithmetic.

title: Worst-case Battleship
words: What is the fewest shots that always sinks the standard fleet on a 10 × 10 board?
math: Compute the minimax number of shots to sink ships of lengths 5,4,3,3,2 on $10\times10$ against an adversary who may move ships consistently with past answers.

title: Sudoku with no smallest puzzle
words: Show the minimum number of clues for an n²×n² Sudoku is asymptotically a fixed fraction of the board.
math: Prove $\min\text{clues}(n)/n^4\to c$ and determine $c$.

title: Mod-3 Collatz escapes
words: For the mod-3 Collatz-like map, almost every starting number should run off to infinity. Prove it.
math: For $h(n)=n/3$ if $3\mid n$, $2n+1$ if $n\equiv1$, $2n-1$ if $n\equiv2\pmod 3$, prove $h^k(n)\to\infty$ for a set of $n$ of natural density 1.

title: Lorenz below threshold
words: The Lorenz weather model becomes chaotic past a known parameter. Prove that just below it there is no strange attractor.
math: For $\sigma=10,\beta=8/3,\rho=24.5$, prove the Lorenz system has no strange attractor (every bounded orbit tends to an equilibrium or periodic orbit, up to measure zero).

title: Emirp sieve
words: Show infinitely many primes have reversals with no small prime factors.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ have $\operatorname{rev}(p)$ with all prime factors $>p^{0.1}$.

title: Seven-free Goldbach for all
words: Show every large even number is a sum of two primes with no digit 7.
math: Prove all sufficiently large even $n$ are sums of two 7-free primes.

title: Prime Nim closed form
words: Find an exact rule for the Prime Nim losing positions that works for every pile size.
math: Give a closed-form characterization of $\{n: G(n)=0\}$ in Prime Nim checkable in $O(\log n)$ arithmetic operations, with proof.

title: Reverse-square map
words: Square a number and reverse its digits; repeat. Show almost every start falls into a loop.
math: For $R(n)=\operatorname{rev}(n^2)$, prove a density-1 set of $n$ has eventually periodic orbits.

title: Primes x² + y³ with prime inputs
words: Show infinitely many primes are a square of a prime plus a cube of a prime.
math: Prove infinitely many primes of the form $p^2+q^3$ with $p,q$ prime.

title: Sudoku resolution bounds
words: Proving a large broken Sudoku has no solution should require long logical proofs.
math: Prove resolution refutations of unsatisfiable $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku instances require size $2^{n^{\Omega(1)}}$ for some explicit family.

title: Chord-graph diameter
words: Chords move to nearby chords by shifting one note one step. How far apart can two chords be?
math: Let $G_{k,m}$ have $k$-subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_m$ as vertices, adjacent when one element moves by $\pm1$. Find $\operatorname{diam}(G_{k,m})$ in closed form.

title: Hat opaque set
words: Find the shortest set of walls that blocks every straight line through the hat tile.
math: Determine the minimal total length of an opaque set for the hat polygon.

title: Lean golf is not approximable
words: Show finding a near-shortest Lean proof is as hard as finding the shortest one, to within any polynomial factor.
math: Prove that approximating minimal Lean 4 proof length within $n^{c}$ for every $c$ is NP-hard.

title: Random-turn Prime Nim
words: In Prime Nim where a coin flip decides who moves, find the exact winning chance from a pile of n.
math: For random-turn play of the prime subtraction game, compute $\lim_n$ of the value from pile $n$, if it exists.

title: Rewrite golf is NP-hard
words: Proving equations by rewriting with commutativity and associativity: finding the shortest rewrite proof should be hard.
math: Prove NP-hardness of deciding whether $s=t$ in a free commutative monoid has a proof of at most $k$ single rewrite steps.

title: Fire whirls
words: Show the equations of buoyant flow allow a rotating column of fire that travels steadily.
math: Prove existence of a smooth traveling swirling solution of the 3D Boussinesq equations with a localized heat source.

title: Fire on a random family tree
words: Fire spreads down a random branching tree. How many firefighters per turn give a fair chance?
math: On a Poisson(2) Galton–Watson tree, find the least constant budget $k$ with $\Pr(\text{contain})>0$ for a fire at the root.

title: Doubly smooth neighbours
words: Find infinitely many primes whose two neighbours have only small prime factors.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $P(p-1),P(p+1)\le p^{0.1}$.

title: Prime squared square
words: Tile a square with smaller squares, all different sizes, every side a prime number. Find one or show none exists.
math: Find a perfect squared square whose component squares all have prime side lengths, or prove none exists.

title: Obtuse sofa
words: The corridor turns 120° instead of 90°. Find a sofa and a matching upper bound within 1%.
math: For a width-1 corridor with turn angle $2\pi/3$, find $A$ with an admissible sofa of area $A$ and a proof that the optimum is $<1.01A$.

title: Unique 3D sofa
words: Show the best solid for a square pipe is unique up to moving it.
math: Prove the optimizer for the $1\times1$ square corridor is unique up to rigid motion.

title: Fractal sofa
words: The corridor walls are Koch-snowflake-like fractals. Show some nonzero area can still get around the corner.
math: For the right-angled corridor with walls replaced by Koch curves of mean width 1, prove the sofa constant is positive and estimate it.

title: Hadwiger counterexample in Lean
words: Give a computer-checked Hadwiger counterexample where the graph is explicitly built, not just proven to exist.
math: Give a Lean 4 term constructing a specific graph $G$ with $h(G)<\chi(G)$, with all quantities computable.

title: Prime-sum circles, square-free gaps
words: Arrange 1 to N in a circle so neighbours add to a prime but never differ by a perfect square.
math: Determine all $N\le200$ admitting a cyclic order of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ with every adjacent sum prime and every adjacent difference a non-square.

title: Prime Golomb rulers
words: Find the shortest ruler with marks only at prime positions where all distances between marks are different.
math: For each $n$, determine the minimal $L$ such that some set of $n$ primes in an interval of length $L$ has all pairwise differences distinct; find its asymptotics.

title: CM Hodge in Lean
words: Check the 2026 AI claim of the Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties with a full computer proof.
math: Formalize in Lean 4 that every rational Hodge class on a CM abelian variety is algebraic.

title: Second-kernel Riemann check
words: Check the 2026 Riemann proof with an independent checker written from scratch, with its own statement of the theorem.
math: Re-verify the 2026 RH proof in a non-Lean kernel (e.g. a new type theory implementation) against an independently written statement, and report agreement.

title: Equal-area triangles in the hat
words: Cut the hat tile into triangles of equal area. Which numbers of triangles are possible?
math: Determine the set of $n$ for which the hat polygon admits a dissection into $n$ triangles of equal area.

title: Graceful forests with one big tree
words: Show a forest is graceful if one tree has more than half the edges.
math: Prove every forest in which some component has more than $m/2$ of the $m$ edges admits a graceful labeling.

title: Smallest-factor Collatz, almost always
words: For the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map, almost every start reaches 1.
math: Prove $g^k(n)=1$ for some $k$, for a density-1 set of $n$.

title: Two-color origami is NP-hard
words: Paper is red on one side and blue on the other. Deciding whether a crease pattern folds flat to show a given picture should be hard.
math: Prove NP-hardness of deciding flat-foldability of a crease pattern subject to a prescribed two-colouring of the visible faces.

title: Hat electrons
words: An electron hopping on a hat tiling should have an unusual, fractal energy spectrum.
math: Prove the tight-binding Hamiltonian on the hat adjacency graph has purely singular continuous spectrum on a set of full measure in the hull.

title: Primes with square digit sum
words: Show infinitely many primes have a digit sum that is a perfect square.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: s_{10}(p)\in\{k^2\}\}\to\infty$, with the expected asymptotic.

title: Doubled twins, almost
words: Show infinitely many primes p have p + 2, 2p + 1 and 2p + 3 each built from a bounded number of primes.
math: Prove there are infinitely many primes $p$ with $\Omega(p+2),\Omega(2p+1),\Omega(2p+3)\le10$.

title: Square-sum cliques
words: How many numbers can pairwise add up to perfect squares? Decide if there is a limit.
math: Decide whether $\omega(S_N)$ is bounded, i.e., whether there exist arbitrarily large sets of distinct positive integers with all pairwise sums square.

title: Prime-sum Latin squares
words: Fill an n × n grid with 1 to n in each row and column so neighbours in a row add to a prime.
math: Determine all $n$ admitting a Latin square on $\{1..n\}$ with all horizontally adjacent sums prime.

title: Primes in orbits
words: Count how many different primes a largest-factor Collatz orbit visits, on average.
math: Prove the average number of distinct primes in $\{f^k(n)\}$ for $n\le x$ is $\sim c\log x$ and compute $c$.

title: Penrose square-sums
words: Number the tiles of a Penrose tiling so neighbouring numbers add to squares. Can it be done for big patches?
math: Decide whether every finite Penrose patch with $N$ tiles admits a bijective labeling by $1..N$ with all adjacent sums square.

title: Firefighter on Z³
words: How many firefighters per turn are needed to contain a fire in 3D, as a precise growth rate?
math: Determine $\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)/t$ for the minimal firefighters needed to contain fire on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ by time $t$.
